_readme: DATED PRICE READINGS FROM PHYSICAL RETAILERS' OWN WEBSITES, one row per
reading. Joined at build time against data/msrp.json for the suggested
figure, and drawn on /retailers.html and on each retailer's own page.
A ROW IS ONE LISTING, OF ONE PRODUCT, ON ONE DAY, AT ONE ADDRESS. It is not
a statement about the company, it is not an average, and it is not current.
build-retailers.mjs prints all of that beside every figure and orders the
table by retailer name, never by the multiple, for the same reason
data/over-msrp.json's _readme gives: sorting by the multiple builds a league
table out of a handful of readings and puts the worst number at the top.
AND IT IS THE FIELD THAT STOPS THIS FILE LIBELLING SOMEBODY. Target, Walmart,
Best Buy and Amazon are a shop and a marketplace at once, so a price on their
site may be the chain's or may be an independent reseller's, and the two are
different claims about different parties. `seller` may only be:
first-party   the chain itself is selling it. Say in `sellerHow` exactly
what on the page establishes that.
marketplace   an independent seller. Evidence about resale, never printed
as what the retailer charges.
There is no third value and there is no blank. A reading whose seller could
not be established is DELETED, not recorded with a hedge. This pass threw
away every price it had gathered from Target and Walmart search pages for
exactly that reason, and Best Buy has no row here at all.
`msrpLabel` NAMES A ROW IN data/msrp.json BY ITS EXACT LABEL and the build
fails if that row does not exist or carries no price. That is the same
discipline resolvePC keeps in build-msrp.mjs, and it is what stops a booster
box being divided by an elite trainer box.
It also means a product with no suggested figure cannot go in here at all.
Meijer's ultra premium collection, CVS's ex battle deck and Staples's
repackaged assortments are all real listings that were read and are not in
this file, because msrp.json prices no row that matches them and inventing a
comparison is worse than having none.
AND A TRUNCATED PRODUCT NAME IS NOT A PRODUCT. Meijer's tiles cut long names
off, so a row reading 'Pokemon Mega Evolution Ascended Heroes Elite' at
$79.99 was left out: it is almost certainly an elite trainer box and almost
certainly is not good enough when the number is going on a page under a
company's name.
`url` is the page the price was read on, and it is a page a reader can open
and check. Every row here was read on a product page rather than a search
result, except where `on` says otherwise, because a search page's price
cannot be checked against later and a product page's can.
NOTHING IS FETCHED FROM pokemoncenter.com BY ANYTHING IN THIS REPO. The
suggested figures come from data/pokemon-center-prices.json, which a person
read by hand in a browser.
